segment.source: Finds broken pages and lost URLs before visitors and search engines do — on any environment, and across a relaunch. Pages and records are recognised by what they are, not by their URL, so a redirect to the wrong content is found as well. Start with Sitemaps; the help says for every finding what it means and who acts on it.

Requests every URL of a snapshot and finds error pages, needless redirects and plugin links that lead nowhere. The URL list may come from another environment: check the larger sitemap of a development system — with news the live site does not have yet — against the live site.
Step 3 — a relaunch without lost URLs

Compares the old and the new website page by page: does every old URL still lead to the same content? A missing redirect is shown with the page it should point at — independent of whether redirects come from the webserver or from TYPO3.
Step 1 — keep the state of a website

Stores the sitemaps of every language as a snapshot. The list of URLs stays, also when the website changes — before a relaunch, it is the only copy of what search engines know. Snapshots can be saved as files and survive a database that is replaced.
For every finding: what it means, whether editors can fix it themselves or the integrator has to, and what to do.
